VisitNotesService.ts is a business (domain) file, and it fails the rule. Its method notesFor has an optional parameter `request?: Request`, and that type comes from the 'express' package. Express is a web framework, so the request type belongs to the delivery/transport layer. The rubric counts it as a violation in a domain signature even when the parameter is optional or unused, as it is here.

The two domain-does-io flags (prisma create and findMany) don't hold up as violations. Those calls go through the injected PrismaService, which the project declares in src/persistence, and the layer model lets business depend on persistence. The rubric says calls into a layer this layer may depend on are not misplaced I/O. The constructor injection of PrismaService is ordinary dependency wiring. The remaining code (trimming text, sorting notes by writtenAt, mapping rows to VisitNote) is domain logic.
